name: Macaroni and cheese (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Macaroni and cheese [Dishes] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 169770 (SR Legacy: 'Macaroni and cheese, box mix with cheese sauce, prepared') - full nutrient panel via nutritionvalue.org and myfooddata.com mirrors
HPLC measurement of carbohydrates and organic acids in cheese varieties (cheddar: lactic 1.44, citric 0.056, acetic 0.23, succinic 0.01, butanoic 0.15 g/100g), PMC10171539
Food-science ingredient analyses of box cheese-sauce mixes (added citric acid + sodium citrate/phosphate acidulant-emulsifiers)
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy source is STARCH (19.4 g/100g) from the pasta; secondary fermentable carbon is lactose (1.3 g/100g) plus cheese-derived lactic and citric acid, which were entirely missing from the FooDB record. Organic-acid amounts are order-of-magnitude estimates scaled from cheddar HPLC data to the dish's cheese fraction (flagged). USDA 169770 provides no measured free-amino-acid profile and no vitamin C/D/K/folate/choline/selenium values, so those are listed present with null amounts.
curation_added: starch 19.4 g/100g (dominant carbon source, was absent as a quantified nutrient)
individual sugars with amounts: lactose 1.3, maltose 0.27, sucrose 0.01 g/100g
organic acids (entirely absent from FooDB): lactic ~0.2, citric ~0.1, acetic ~0.03 g/100g
L-valine and L-phenylalanine (missing from FooDB amino-acid list)
quantified vitamins (A, B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12, E) and minerals (Na, P, Ca, K, Mg, Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu)

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
